Counsel for Applicant :- Dilip Kumar Singh Chauhan
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Karunesh Singh Pawar,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA for the State and perused the record.
None appears on behalf of the complainant.
In the FIR it is alleged that the applicant called the prosecutrix at Koyla Dhal and from there he took her to Chandrika Devi temple gate where his friends Abhishek and Saurabh were there.
Awadhesh was also there.
Awadhesh went away from there and thereafter the remaining accused persons took her to Oyo Hotel of Bakshi Ka Talaab where they raped her.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the prosecutrix in her statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. has repeated the prosecution version as narrated in the FIR.
While giving statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., no allegation of rape has been leveled against the applicant.
The victim has been examined before the trial court and during her cross examination, she has again not alleged any Abhishek Rajpoot @ Tota Ram vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home ...

Since the victim has been examined before the trial court, there is no chance of tampering the evidence.
It has been further submitted that on the basis of a transfer certificate, the case has been registered under the POCSO Act.
Deliberately, victim's ossification test has not been conducted by the investigating officer.
The victim is major and the transfer certificate cannot be the basis for ascertaining the age of the minor in view of the Section 94 of J.J. Act.
It is further submitted that the applicant is languishing in jail since 13.07.2023 without having any criminal antecedent.
There is no possibility of the applicant of fleeing away after being released from jail or tampering with the witnesses.
In case the applicant is enlarged on bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail.

Learned AGA has opposed the bail application, however, could not dispute the fact that the victim has not taken name of the applicant in her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. and the victim has been examined before the trial court.

On due consideration to the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.; lack of corroborative material, coupled with the fact that the applicant is languishing in jail since 13.07.2023 without having any criminal antecedent and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I find it to be a fit case for enlarging the applicant on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant, Abhishek Rajpoot @ Tota Ram, involved in Case Crime/FIR No. 260/2023, under Sections 376-DA IPC, Section 3(2)(v) of SC/ST Act and under Section 5G/6 of POCSO Act, Police Station - Bakshi Ka Talaab, District - Lucknow, be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
(ii) The applicant will not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness.
(iii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iv) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
